sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy; unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state fiscal distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Code civil and Code de commerce basis, strongly harmonised with EU company law and GDPR)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States bilateral investment treaty (in force since 1991)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties with third states (including China and the United Arab Emirates)
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force since 1 February 2019)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (provisionally applicable since 21 September 2017)
Luxembourg-Germany double taxation agreement (2012, in force since 2013)
United States-Luxembourg double taxation convention (signed 1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg-France and Luxembourg-Netherlands double taxation agreements (as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, including by the Law of 25 March 2020 implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (SARL provisions); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and company accounting; Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 and CSSF AML/CFT circulars; EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on funds transfer information; FATF Recommendations 10, 12, 24 and 25; CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (22 November 2022), in consequence of which unrestricted public remote access to the RBE is suspended, access being reserved to competent authorities and AML-obligated entities acting on validated legitimate-interest requests.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder: certificate of incorporation and extract from the relevant commercial register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder: certificate of good standing (status certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or tax administration of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual UBO/shareholder: current passport copy and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority / utility or bank issuer of the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (or certified true copy accepted by the notary for standard profiles)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation, where shareholders act through a representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the representative's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration (declaration de beneficiaire effectif) for RBE registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not applicable - declaration submitted directly by the notary on the RBE portal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation (French or German) of foreign-language corporate and banking documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-sworn translator in the country of origin or Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation attachment to the apostillised original (Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at notary mandate and again at bank account opening of all UBOs, directors, managers and authorised signatories against: (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions list (EU Regulations 765/2006, 269/2014 and 881/2002, as updated), (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists, (iii) OFAC SDN list given the USD payment rails and (iv) Luxembourg Ministry of Finance asset-freeze decisions; PEP identification under Article 1 of the 2004 AML Law consistent with FATF Recommendation 12, EBA Guidelines 2021/02 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; a documented source-of-funds analysis is required for any PEP-matched or high-reputation-risk profile; the low criminal-risk tier of the ISIC 4791 e-commerce model does not disapply standard customer due diligence, which remains mandatory with risk-based simplified measures permitted only within the statutory framework.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal (Guichet.lu / lbr.lu) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin-alphabet characters; French, German, English and Luxembourgish denominations are accepted; the legal-form suffix 'S.a r.l.' or 'Sarl' is mandatory; each name must be distinctive and not create confusion with names already registered in the RCS, names protected by EU or national IP instruments, or names capable of misleading the public as to legal form, nationality or regulated activity; non-Latin (e.g., Cyrillic, Mandarin) trade expressions must be transliterated and filed alongside the Latin main name, with the Latin form being decisive for the RCS index.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The LBR-issued non-confusion certificate is valid for 60 days and is not extendable; if rejected, the applicant may immediately resubmit up to three ranked name variants through the notary at no additional LBR charge; a formal refusal must be appealed in writing to the LBR central registry within one month of notification, and any dismissal of the objection may be brought before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) under the regime of the Law of 19 December 2002; parallel pre-screen against EUIPO and Luxembourg IPI trademark registers is recommended to avoid post-incorporation rebranding.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the ISIC 4791/NAICS 458110 fast-fashion e-commerce model under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, provided the domiciliation agent is a supervised professional (approved bank, notary, audit firm or licensed professional domiciliation company); the 1999 Law requires the agent to maintain physical access to corporate records and to communicate promptly on inspections; no dedicated sectorial licence is required for distance retailing of apparel and footwear; thus a virtual office fulfils the registered-office obligation and is acceptable to the RCS, the RBE, the VAT administration (AEDT) and payment-service providers using Klarna and Shopify Payments rails.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the first three operating years: quantified at approximately 3% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection of the registered office in the base retail e-commerce scenario; the probability increases to 8-12% where treaty benefits are claimed for e-commerce intangibles or where the registered agent handles multiple unrelated companies; the residence and substance risk is mitigated by retaining lease or domiciliation agreements, bank statements, books and e-commerce platform contracts at the registered office address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and statutory capital verification for SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and prevailing market fee for a standard SARL at EUR 12,000 minimum capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name screening and negative non-confusion certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated LBR fee schedule (same-day electronic issuance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the company and filing of the draft articles in the RCS
Publication of incorporation in the Recueil electronique des societes et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory publication fee for electronic filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service (prorated first three months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual package EUR 2,000-3,500 (prorated for pre-incorporation budget)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account or payment-services account onboarding (KYC, beneficial-owner forms, sanctions re-screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff and PSP onboarding benchmark (Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments compatible)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees - drafting articles of association, shareholders' agreement, board resolutions and AML file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed fee for a standard single-shareholder or shareholder-group SARL)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 180-192 et seq. governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée 'SARL'); Law of 23 December 2016 on minimum share capital and SME amendments; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Business Registers and the RESA electronic gazette.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 15 Boulevard Joseph II, L-1840 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Acte de Constitution) containing the coordinated Articles of Association (Statuts Coordonnés), executed by a Luxembourg notary and filed electronically with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of a SARL is EUR 12,000 (Law of 10 August 1915 as amended in 2016). At least 25% of each cash share (minimum EUR 3,000 in aggregate) must be paid up at incorporation, while in-kind contributions must be fully paid up; the subscribed cash capital must be blocked on a dedicated account with a Luxembourg credit institution pending RCS registration, evidenced by a capital blocking certificate. Alternatively, under the Law of 23 December 2016, a SARL may be formed with fully paid-up cash capital between EUR 1 and EUR 12,000, subject to a statutory auditor's report and certain restrictions on share transfers and distributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] SARL, adopted on [DATE] after incorporation under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies. RESOLVED: (1) the subscription, allotment and cash payment of the Company's entire share capital of EUR 12,000 is ratified; (2) the registered office at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg, is adopted as the statutory seat, effective upon RCS registration; (3) [NAME] is appointed first manager (gérant), holding sole signature authority to represent the Company in all acts within its corporate object; (4) the manager is instructed to maintain books, file all RCS and fiscal declarations, and procure VAT registration; (5) prior acts of the incorporator for the Company's benefit are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Check and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - online name reservation portal (www.lbr.lu / RCS e-services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for a corporate name ending in 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'. The request must demonstrate that the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to existing RCS-registered entities and does not conflict with registered trademarks. Upon approval, the LBR issues a name reservation certificate valid for two months, renewable for a further two months, which must be annexed to the notarized deed.
required_dossiers: Completed online name reservation form
Passport or identity document of the applicant
Declaration of proposed corporate purpose (ISIC 4791 e-commerce retailing)
Optional trademark search report for the proposed brand name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity, file an administrative contestation with the LBR or amend the name; if a third party opposes, execute an amending name disclaimer or select a secondary distinctive name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, BCEE/Spuerkeess)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional blocked account in the name of the future SARL ('Société en formation'). Transfer the full subscribed cash capital (EUR 12,000 or, in the reduced-capital regime, the agreed amount fully paid). The bank must issue an attestation de blocage confirming that the funds are deposited and irrevocably unavailable until the RCS registration is completed. This certificate is a mandatory annex to the notarized deed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Passport copies of all shareholders and prospective manager(s)
Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC documentation
Source of funds evidence and bank references
Certificate of incorporation of corporate shareholders or statutory declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a KYC query, provide additional source-of-wealth documentation, audited financial statements or a notarized affidavit; if the bank declines, transfer funds to an alternative Luxembourg credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarized Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the chosen notary with all shareholders or their authorized representatives. The notary verifies legal capacity, incorporation formalities, the capital blocking certificate, and the legality of the corporate purpose. The notary reads and executes the deed containing the articles of association (corporate name, registered office, object, share capital, manager appointment, and duration), and obtains the manager's signed acceptance and declaration of no criminal disqualification.
required_dossiers: Valid capital blocking certificate from the bank
Power of attorney for each shareholder representative (if applicable)
Passport copies and residency proof of shareholders and managers
Coordinated draft articles of association
Financial plan (mandatory for reduced capital below EUR 12,000)
Name reservation certificate from LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, execute a correcting addendum (acte rectificatif) before the same notary; if a shareholder fails to appear, reschedule and obtain a fresh power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with RCS and Publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - electronic filing filed by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the notarized deed and the legally required annexes with the RCS through the LBR electronic filing system within one month of execution. The RCS assigns a corporate registration number; the deed or an extract is published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). Legal personality is effective on the date of RCS registration, and the company's liability regime and third-party effects attach from publication.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Capital blocking certificate
Manager's signed acceptance and certificate of good conduct (extraits du casier judiciaire if requested)
RCS registration application form
Statement of compliance with anti-money-laundering (Law of 12 November 2004)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query requesting additional documents, supply the missing particulars within the prescribed deadline; the registration remains valid retroactively if the cure is filed in time, otherwise file a supplementary registration correcting the record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security and Beneficial Owner Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines (AED), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the RCS extract, file the corporate registration for corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal). Register for VAT through the Guichet Unique (RBE) to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number (early registration recommended for e-commerce). File the mandatory beneficial ownership declaration with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) within one month. If any employee will be hired, enrol the company and staff with the CCSS using the online MySocialSecurity portal.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarized articles of association
Lease agreement or proof of registered office address
Identity documents and address of all managers and shareholders
Beneficial ownership declaration form (RBE)
Employer registration forms (if hiring)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration requests clarifications, file the missing documents online and respond within the stated period; late VAT registration may attract an administrative fine but can be cured by an 'régularisation' with the AED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Operating Bank Account and Payment Services Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution and Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for any regulated payment activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convert the provisional blocked account into an active operating current account upon presentation of the RCS extract and final articles. Complete the bank's final KYC and signatory mandate. For the fast-fashion e-commerce rails (Shopify Payments, Klarna BNPL), use the payment institutions' standard PSP integration; verify that no Luxembourg payment-e-money licence is triggered because the company merely sells goods and does not receive deposits within the meaning of the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarized articles of association
Signatory mandate list and identity documents of authorised persons
Business plan or financial projections
PSP and BNPL processing agreements (Shopify Payments, Klarna)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced AML scrutiny, file the upstream group structure and provenance of funds; if the bank refuses, select an alternative licensed institution; the use of PCI-DSS compliant PSPs avoids any additional CSSF licensing exposure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to occupations, the electronic retailing of fast-fashion apparel and footwear (ISIC 4791) does not appear on the list of regulated trades requiring an establishment authorization from the Direction Générale des PME of the Ministry of the Economy. A physical retail store, if subsequently opened, would be subject to municipal commercial occupation rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial operating permit (autorisation d'établissement) is required for a pure e-commerce apparel retailer operating solely through a warehouse/fulfillment arrangement and online storefront.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No EIA is required for pure electronic retailing. If the company operates a warehouse or fulfillment centre with a floor area above 500 m², a 'Commodo/Incommode' declaration under the Law of 10 June 1999 (class 4 or 5) may be triggered, but no full Environmental Impact Assessment is expected.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for office-only retail operations; any operational wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge rules (RGD of 9 July 2014); packaging waste from returned or shipped goods must be managed under the EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC and the Luxembourg packaging law (Law of 21 March 2017); any marketed textiles and footwear must comply with REACH (EC 1907/2006) restricted substances and the EU Textile Regulation (EU 1007/2011).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the competent municipal authority is required for staffed premises such as offices and warehouses; the Groupement d'Intervention du Service National de la Protection Civile (CGDIS) conducts technical inspections for higher-risk sites. Occupational clearance: comply with the Luxembourg Labour Code and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) standards covering work equipment, electrical installations, ergonomics, emergency exits and first-aid provisions. A 'déclaration de mise en exploitation' must be filed with the municipal authority before occupying any warehousing or office space.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; unified e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) and the AEDT business portal (https://pbl.etat.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCSL), the RCSL automatically notifies the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax registration. For VAT, the SARL (or a foreign entity making taxable supplies in Luxembourg) must file Form 640 'Déclaration d'identification à la TVA' with the AEDT, either via MyGuichet.lu electronic filing or in writing, before commencing taxable activity. The application requires: a copy of the articles of association (statuts) and RCSL extract, proof of the managing director's identity, a signed power of attorney, and a description of taxable activities. Non-established foreign e-commerce sellers without a Luxembourg fixed establishment may alternatively register under the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme for intra-EU distance sales rather than obtaining a full Luxembourg VAT ID; however, sales from local stock (fulfilment warehouse in Luxembourg) always require direct VAT registration. Standard processing time is 10-15 business days. VAT number format: LU + 8 digits for legal entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election; SARLs are inherently opaque and subject to full corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), and net wealth tax (NWT). Available statutory elections: (i) Luxembourg VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT Law allowing financially, economically, and organisationally linked resident entities to file VAT as a single taxpayer; (ii) Luxembourg tax consolidation (régime d'intégration fiscale) for direct taxation of 95%-owned resident or EU subsidiaries; (iii) EU OSS non-Union scheme election for intra-EU distance sales of fast-fashion goods; (iv) option to apply Luxembourg VAT to certain real estate transactions; (v) election for the small-business franchise exemption (franchise en base) for turnover below EUR 35,000, subject to a waiver of input VAT deduction. Hybrid mismatch elections follow ATAD I and II implementation in the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR Articles 168bis and 168ter).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small businesses (franchise en base); EUR 10,000 pan-EU threshold for intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers (below the threshold Luxembourg VAT at 17% applies; above the threshold the destination country's VAT applies via the OSS); no registration threshold for foreign suppliers operating from a Luxembourg warehouse or performing supplies in Luxembourg - they must register from the first euro of taxable sales in the absence of an applicable exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate exists for B2B/B2C e-commerce invoicing. Luxembourg mandates B2G e-invoicing via the PEPPOL network (PEPPOL BIS 3.0) for invoices to central government entities since 1 January 2021, with extension to municipal and wider public sector bodies under EU Directive 2014/55/EU. There are no API-based tax authority clearance requirements, no SAF-T periodic filing mandate (SAF-T only on request), and no mandatory digital invoice stamping in Luxembourg. VAT returns and recapitulative statements (Intrastat/EC Sales Lists) are filed electronically via the AEDT e-TVA/MDG portal. XML/UBL e-invoicing for B2B remains voluntary, but the VIDA (VAT in the Digital Age) proposal may introduce structured e-invoicing by 2028.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to: (i) exports of fast-fashion apparel and footwear dispatched or transported by the seller or on his behalf to a destination outside the European Union, evidenced by a customs export declaration (SAD) and proof that the goods left the EU within 90 days of supply; (ii) directly connected services such as international transport, loading, warehousing, and freight forwarding ancillary to those exports; (iii) supplies to non-EU customers of goods exported under the 'exporter's possession' rule provided the exporter is established at the EU, holds title, and retains full documentation per the Luxembourg VAT Circular N°703. Qualification requires that the supplier retain the original export invoice, the CMR/air waybill/Bill of Lading, the customs entry certificate, and a bank transfer or payment receipt demonstrating payment from the non-EU principal. For distance sales to EU consumers, standard destination-country VAT via OSS (or 17% Luxembourg VAT below the threshold) applies; goods imported into third countries (e.g., UK, USA) require VAT/customs duties of that jurisdiction and are not zero-rated under Luxembourg rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Single Administrative Document (SAD) or automated export e-entry filed in the Luxembourg customs system (LuxTrade/ICS-ECS)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical transport out of the EU within 90 days (Circular TVA N°703/704)
Commercial invoice and proforma invoice matching quantities, values, HS codes, and consignee details
Certificate of Export (certificat d'exportation) issued/proof of customs exit from the competent customs office
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT and bank statement evidencing payment from the non-EU buyer; foreign exchange conversion records when payment is in a non-EUR currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg AEDT and customs conduct targeted audits of cross-border fast-fashion e-commerce models. Zero-rating is invalidated retroactively if documentary proof is incomplete or if the goods are diverted to EU consumption; the VAT due at 17% is clawed back with default interest at 0.6% per month. Non-fraudulent documentary errors attract administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 and a 10% late-payment penalty. Fraudulently claimed export exemptions (false invoicing, merchandise circulation schemes) are subject to criminal sanctions: VAT fraud fines of up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years, publication of judgments, exclusion from public contracts, and personal joint liability of directors; the statutory reassessment period is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of tax fraud or wilful misdeclaration. Repatriation delay beyond 180 days without commercial justification is treated by tax audit as a permanent establishment indicator and may trigger transfer pricing adjustments under the Luxembourg TP Guidelines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem, and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent authority for banking licensing, payment institutions, electronic money institutions, and AML/CTF supervision. The BCL compiles national balance-of-payments statistics and transmits monetary and financial data to the European Central Bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full and unrestricted euro convertibility on both current and capital account transactions pursuant to Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the free movement of capital and payments regime, transposed into Luxembourg law without exchange-control authorizations. Retail e-commerce receipts, trade settlements, shareholder loans, and capital injections may be freely converted and remitted. No profit-repatriation licensing or administrative approval is required; the only prudential hurdles are the bank's transaction documentation standards under CSSF AML regulations and, for dividend distributions, the applicable dividend withholding tax (standard 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate shareholder holds at least 10% of share capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or timing requirement applies to export proceeds in Luxembourg. Receivables from cross-border fast-fashion sales may be retained indefinitely in EUR or any foreign currency in an account at a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution, subject to the bank's balance-of-payment statistical declarations and applicable EU sanctions and asset-freeze screening obligations under Council Regulation (EU) No 765/2006 and Luxembourg implementing measures.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for payment execution, multi-currency settlement, and API-driven FX interfaces, but Low for core treasury liquidity because balances at EMIs are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme. An electronic money institution or payment institution authorized in an EEA state and passported into Luxembourg under the Luxembourg Law of 10 July 2018 implementing PSD2 may lawfully provide IBANs, cross-border collections, and FX conversion; however, the SARL should maintain the primary operating treasury and capital escrow at a Tier-1 commercial bank, using EMI rails only for subordinated disbursement workstreams.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 23 August 2000 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, the bank must identify and verify the identity of the customer, the beneficial owners, and the authorized signatories. In practice, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one physical or high-assurance video-verified interview with the managing director and the UBOs prior to account opening; a simple online form is not sufficient. Remote opening is legally possible where the bank applies an eIDAS-qualified electronic signature or a regulated video-KYC process, but the initial board resolution appointing the account signatories, the notarized incorporation deed, and specimen signatures must be delivered in physical or notarially certified form to remove onboarding blockers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border receipts from e-commerce and BNPL payment channels (Klarna, Shopify Payments) with no direct traceability to a physical retail footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed current business plan for the fast-fashion e-commerce operation, executed merchant services agreements with Shopify and Klarna, settlement statements reconciling customer-side payments to treasury inflows, the SARL's return and refund policy, and a written anti-money-laundering and transaction-monitoring procedure for the entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholders or opaque beneficial ownership chain in the SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association of the SARL, share register evidencing full capital subscription and payment, extract from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and Luxembourg Business Registers, UBO declaration, an organizational chain-of-ownership chart, certificate of tax residence of each corporate shareholder, and a source-of-wealth declaration from the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Procurement from apparel suppliers domiciled in high-risk or sanctions-sensitive jurisdictions (e.g., Bangladesh, Vietnam, Turkey, China) with risks of trade-based money laundering or dual-use goods misdeclaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original purchase orders and supplier agreements incorporating Incoterms 2020, supplier invoices with detailed HS code and SKU references, customs import and export declarations, evidence of screening of suppliers against EU and UN sanctions lists, and a supplier KYC questionnaire including beneficial ownership of each vendor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated payment reversals, chargebacks, or BNPL disputes that could indicate origination-related fraud or layering of merchant funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chargeback and dispute ledger reconciling Shopify Payments, Klarna and card-scheme reports, the SARL's published online terms and conditions, a refund SLA signed with the fulfilment provider, and a cash-flow model demonstrating that reversals remain immaterial and are funded exclusively from ordinary operating receipts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholders must wire the SARL's share capital, being at least EUR 12,000 for a standard SARL, by SWIFT MT103 in EUR to the dedicated capital escrow account at the onboarding bank, citing SWIFT purpose code EQUI (equity) or INTR (intra-group transfer). The bank will evidence receipt through a confirmation statement used by the notary in the incorporation file. For shareholder loans exceeding the equity injection, a written shareholder loan agreement and a board resolution authorizing the debt are required; the receiving bank will classify the transaction as a direct investment or intercompany loan for BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting, ensuring full compliance with EU capital movement free-flow provisions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EEA and Eurozone suppliers, the clearing rail is SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 XML (pain.001.001.09) with the SARL's IBAN and the supplier's IBAN, avoiding FX conversion and SWIFT fees. For non-EEA apparel and logistics providers in Asia or the Americas, the rail is SWIFT MT103 bank-to-bank telegraphic transfer in EUR, USD, GBP, or CNY, quoting the commercial invoice and order number in the payment narrative. For high-value garment purchase contracts, an irrevocable, confirmed documentary letter of credit (MT700) is recommended, issued by the SARL's Luxembourg bank in favor of the supplier's confirming bank, with the L/C, invoices, booking notes, and certificates of origin aligned under Incoterms 2020.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forward (EUR against USD, GBP, CNY, or CHF) executed bilaterally with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution or a CSSF-registered investment firm under ISDA and EMIR clearing protocols.

Non-deliverable FX forward (NDF) for hedging purchases denominated in restricted or non-convertible currencies such as INR, BDT, PKR, or VND, where the underlying exposure is a documented firm purchase order and the tenor matches the forecast payable.
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) for medium-term shareholder loans or asset-based financing, converting floating-rate foreign currency debt into EUR fixed-rate exposure.

FX swap / spot-forward rollover for operational liquidity bridging between the Schengen treasury account and the offshore or foreign-currency settlement accounts, subject to the bank's conduct controls and without speculative open positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS annual confirmation of corporate data (confirmation annuelle au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 1 month of the registration anniversary (Art. 3A, Law of 19 December 2002); electronic filing via LBR RCS e-file portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder and public default annotation by LBR; managers exposed to criminal fines under Art. 31 of the Law of 19 December 2002; two consecutive missed confirmations can trigger judicial dissolution proceedings before the Luxembourg district court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RBE annual UBO confirmation (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after each anniversary of the initial RBE declaration (Law of 13 January 2019; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 March 2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalty of EUR 500 to EUR 1,250,000 and/or imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years under Art. 8 of the Law of 13 January 2019; outdated UBO records visible to the Luxembourg FIU (CRF) may trigger enhanced due diligence or account restrictions by regulated financial intermediaries.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) with statutory auditor's report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS; publication in the official electronic compendium (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end (shareholders' approval within 6 months, deposit within 1 month after approval); for a 31 December year-end: deposit by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers individually liable to criminal fines of EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 under Art. 31 of the Law of 19 December 2002; RCS record annotated for default; repeated non-filing may lead to court-ordered judicial dissolution and loss of good-standing certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate tax return (CIT, municipal business tax, net wealth tax) and minimum net wealth tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end: filing by 31 December of the following calendar year (6-month statutory period plus administrative blanket extension); e-filing via MyGuichet/eCAB
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% on assessed tax and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; ACD may issue an ex officio assessment after formal notice; aggravated non-filing exposes corporate officers to criminal fines of up to EUR 1,000 and collection enforcement on bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary annual shareholders' meeting (approval of annual accounts and discharge of managers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate organ; minutes retained in the statutory minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end: by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting invalidates the lawful approval of the accounts; distributions made without approved accounts are recoverable from managers as unauthorized distributions; managers cannot obtain a valid discharge for their management of the fiscal year.
